reason: The goal is to make a muscle fibre shorten, so I’ll start by bringing its thin and thick filaments together.
expectation: I expect a filament arrangement that can help the fibre contract, though it may still need energy and a calcium signal.

alternatives.reason: Making usable energy also seems necessary, but I want to assemble the pulling structures first.

effect: The overlapping filaments form sliding units; I’ll now build the fibre that can contain them.
reaction: The overlap makes the assembly plausible, though the result does not yet explain how it pulls.
reason: Combining the cell and fibre structures seems like the next step toward assembling a muscle fibre.
expectation: I expect a muscle fibre with the sugar transporter in its membrane, but it may still need the filament units and energy.

alternatives.reason: Making usable energy also looks necessary, but I want to assemble the fibre first.

effect: The muscle fibre provides a scaffold with spaces for the filament units, so I can assemble them next.
reaction: The spaces make the next fitting easy to understand.
reason: I want to put the sliding units into the fibre to build its shortening machinery.
expectation: I expect a fibre containing the filament units, though it may still need energy and a calcium signal to shorten.

alternatives.reason: The fibre will also need usable energy, but I want to finish assembling its structures first.

effect: The fibre now contains the filament units; the remaining offered combination appears to begin supplying energy.
reaction: The assembly is clear, though it has not yet shown how the filaments produce movement.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and glucose and oxygen suggest a route toward usable energy.
expectation: I expect a product related to releasing energy from glucose, perhaps a step toward making ATP.

effect: Glucose is split in the cell fluid before smaller fuel molecules enter the mitochondrion, where oxygen also arrives. The next step appears to make ATP.
reaction: The picture clarifies that the initial splitting happens outside the mitochondrion.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and joining ADP and phosphate appears to be the route to usable energy.
expectation: I expect the fuelled mitochondria to help produce ATP from ADP and phosphate.

effect: The mitochondria produced an ATP supply, with ADP and phosphate returning as ATP is used. I can now connect that supply to the fibre.
reaction: The return arrows make the continuing energy cycle clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the fibre needs ATP for its pulling machinery.
expectation: I expect an ATP-supplied muscle fibre, though it may still need the calcium signal to shorten.

effect: ATP is now available at the fibre’s filaments; the calcium signal appears to be the remaining step toward shortening.
reaction: The progression is clear, though I am still curious how the filaments pull.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and calcium appears to signal the fibre to contract.
expectation: I expect the calcium signal to enable the ATP-ready fibre to shorten, perhaps with an explanation of how its filaments move.

effect: The calcium signal completed the fibre, and the result shows that its filaments slide past each other while keeping their length.
reaction: The comparison of the two poses finally makes the shortening mechanism clear and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding calcium was the most worthwhile action because the result showed how sliding filaments shorten the fibre without shortening themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Supplying ATP to the fibre felt like a predictable intermediate step; its result showed ATP at the filaments but did not yet explain their movement.

surprise.text: The fibre shortens even though the individual filaments stay the same length.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though several intermediate combinations were predictable and the menu supplied their compatibility.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how shortening fibres contribute to movement at the tissue and body-system level, especially if later results explain those connections as clearly as the final sliding picture.
